title: Native Japanese prompt baseline
question: How much can explicit Japanese speaking guidance improve correctness and perceived naturalness without replacing native realtime audio?
hypothesis: A specific Japanese prompt will improve language stability, pacing, and operational readings while preserving native response and interruption latency, but it will not fully solve pitch accent and proper-noun failures.

control.description: Native realtime voice with the current default prompt.

variants.description: Native realtime voice with explicit language, accent, mora, pause, number, and pronunciation guidance.

environment.runtime: TBD: ChatGPT Web or supported realtime client and version
environment.hardware: TBD: browser, OS, audio device, and DaaS path

procedure.summary: Render the same randomized smoke utterances under control and prompt variants, collect timing traces, then run blinded Japanese correctness and preference review.
procedure.warmup: TBD: define session and audio warmup before timing samples.
invalidation_conditions: The fixture manifest or prompt changes after approval.
Control and variant use different model or voice revisions.
Audio routing records the same output twice or clips a material segment.
Raters can infer the variant label from filenames or presentation order.

decision_rule: Advance the prompt variant as the new baseline only if blinded preference and operational-reading accuracy improve without a material regression in response start, interruption, or language stability. Freeze exact thresholds before approval.

artifact_policy.git_contents: Plan, redacted fixture manifest, aggregate metrics, failure taxonomy, and decision only.
artifact_policy.authorization: Synthetic prompts; any captured voice output follows the applicable account and evaluation policy.
